examples.problem:
What is the minor of $c_{22}$ in the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}7x & 0 & -3y \\ 1 & x+2y & 4 \\ -y & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and second column: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}7x & ∗ & -3y \\ ∗ & x+2y & ∗ \\ -y & ∗ & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}7x & -3y \\ -y & 5\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}7x & -3y \\ -y & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =7x\cdot 5-(-3y)\cdot (-y) \\  & =35x-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
For the matrix
$C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 7 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}].$
find the minor ${M}_{12}$ of the entry ${c}_{12}.$

${M}_{12}=${{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The minor of ${c}_{12}=2$ (first row, second column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $2$ are removed: 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 2 & ∗ \\ 0 & ∗ & 4 \\ 7 & ∗ & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${c}_{12}=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{12} & =\text{det}[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot 6-4\cdot 7 \\  & =0-28 \\  & =-28.\end{aligned}
$$
